title: Evidence-Based Reading — The Night Shift
description: Practice making an inference, then choosing the evidence that proves it.
subject: rla
author: Chee Skool
reviewNotes: Migrated from the Phase 3C runtime module without changing the learner-facing skill family. Reclassified out of learner Passage Practice during Reading Quality Refinement V1 because the text is a short cross-track prototype, not a GED-length transfer passage.

questions.prompt: What is the best description of Maria's feelings about the night shift?

options.text: She has grown to prefer it.
She resents it but has no other choice.
options.whyWrong: The passage never shows resentment. It says she likes the quiet and chooses to stay.
Maria is not neutral. The passage gives several details showing that she likes the night shift.

options.text: She is actively trying to leave it.
options.whyWrong: Nothing says Maria is trying to leave. Other workers leave for daytime jobs, but Maria stays.

explanation.whyCorrect: Maria likes the quiet and stays even when other workers leave. Those details show that she has grown to prefer the night shift.
explanation.quickTip: For a feelings question, use what the character does and what the passage says they like.

questions.prompt: Which sentence from the passage best supports the idea that Maria's real reason for staying isn't about money?

options.text: She liked the quiet of it — the hum of the conveyor belts, the empty parking lot...
options.whyWrong: This shows that Maria likes the shift, but it does not directly prove that money is not her real reason.

options.text: She told her sister it was because night shift paid a premium, but the truth was simpler.
Her coworkers came and went, chasing daytime hours and better pay, but Maria stayed.
options.whyWrong: This compares Maria with her coworkers, but it does not directly reveal why her stated reason is not the real one.

options.text: Maria had worked the night shift at the packing plant for six years.
options.whyWrong: This is true, but it only gives background information. It does not answer why Maria really stays.

explanation.whyCorrect: The sentence contrasts what Maria says with 'the truth.' That directly shows that money is not her real reason.
explanation.quickTip: For evidence questions, pick the line that proves the claim—not just a line about the same topic.

curriculum.learningObjective: Make an inference from passage details and choose the sentence that directly supports it.
